# Design: Specify four behaviors that shipped without a spec

## Context

All four behaviors are already in the code. This change writes specs for
them and nothing else. Each spec maps to the code and tests below.

| Spec requirement | Code | Existing test |
|---|---|---|
| `decisions` — ADRs with Windows line endings | `codev-core/src/decisions/parser.rs` (`extract_frontmatter`, `find_close_fence`); `codev-core/src/decisions/seal.rs` (`body_slice`); `codev-engine/src/decisions_actions.rs` (`rewrite_frontmatter_status`) | `a_crlf_adr_is_parsed_like_an_lf_one`, `hash_with_crlf_is_supported`, `rewriting_the_status_keeps_a_crlf_body_byte_for_byte` |
| `docs` — Warning callouts in the offline HTML | `codev-cli/src/docs.rs` (`mark_warning_callouts`, `WARNING_TITLES`); `codev-cli/assets/docs.css` (`blockquote.warning`) | `warning_callouts_get_their_own_class` |
| `docs` — `--print` exits quietly when its reader goes away | `codev-cli/src/main.rs`, `Command::Docs` branch (`ErrorKind::BrokenPipe` → 0) | none found |
| `init` — inherited paths use forward slashes | `codev-cli/src/commands.rs` (`resolve_inherits`, `absolute`, `clean`, `portable`) | `init_writes_inherits_and_pins_git_sources` (covers `../home/shared` → `/home/shared`; does not cover Windows separators) |

Decisions that constrain the specs:

- 0001 (functional core, imperative shell): the frontmatter rewrite is
  computed as text and written through an effect plan. The spec states the
  result and not that mechanism, which is the level the project's rule
  for specs asks for.
- 0005 (read-only inherited sources): the `init` requirement covers only
  the paths written to `config.yaml`. It does not change how inherited
  sources are read.

## Goals / Non-Goals

Goals:

- Every observable part of the four behaviors is in a spec, at the level
  of what users see: exit codes, file contents, rendering.

Non-goals:

- Changing any behavior, aligning code with any other component, or
  adding tests. A missing test is recorded below as a risk. Adding it
  would need a separate change, since this request is limited to
  documentation.

## Decisions

### Decision: Add each behavior as an `ADDED` requirement

The four behaviors are new concerns next to existing requirements. For
example, `--print` already has a requirement for its normal output. Using
`ADDED` leaves those requirements untouched.

**Alternatives considered**: a `MODIFIED` block on
`` `codev docs --print` prints the markdown source to stdout `` and on
`` `codev init --inherit` declares inherited sources ``. It was rejected
because a `MODIFIED` block has to copy the whole requirement, which risks
losing detail when the change is archived. It would also make reviewers
re-read text that has not changed.

### Decision: The specs follow the code, not its comments or its neighbours

Where the code and its surroundings disagree, the spec describes what the
code does. The offline HTML treats only `**Warning**` and `**Attention**`,
matched exactly, as warning titles, even though the comment in `docs.rs`
says it uses "the same set the website's theme recognizes".

**Alternatives considered**: specifying the website's larger set
(`docs/theme/mairistem.js` also accepts `Caution`, `Important` and
`Avertissement`, in any case and with a trailing `:` or `.`). It was
rejected because the specs would then describe a behavior the binary does
not have, which turns a documentation change into a behavior change.

### Decision: Seal normalization stays out of the spec

The spec fixes where a CRLF body starts and requires that the body comes
through a status rewrite unchanged. It does not say whether the seal hash
normalizes line endings. Today it does not: `hash_with_crlf_is_supported`
notes that the hash "differs from a pure LF one … documented as a risk".

**Alternatives considered**: specifying "the hash is computed on the raw
bytes, with no normalization". It was rejected because it would make the
risk below a contract. Whether to normalize is a behavior decision for a
change of its own.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [`--print`'s quiet exit and the Windows separators have no dedicated
  test, so the new specs can be broken without a test failing] →
  Mitigation: listed here so that a follow-up change adds a CLI test that
  pipes `codev docs --print` into `head`, and a test of `portable` on a
  path with `\`. The new scenarios are written so they can become those
  tests directly.
- [The seal hash is not normalized: a decision sealed on an LF checkout
  and checked out on Windows with `core.autocrlf=true` gets CRLF line
  endings, and `codev validate` would report `decision_seal_mismatch`] →
  Mitigation: kept out of the spec on purpose (see the decision above) and
  raised as an open question. It needs a change of its own if it is
  confirmed.
- [The offline HTML and the website treat warning titles differently, so
  `> **Caution**` is a warning online and a note offline] → Mitigation:
  the spec names the two titles explicitly, so the difference is visible.
  Aligning the two is an open question.

## Open Questions

- Should the seal normalize line endings (CRLF → LF) before hashing, so
  that a seal survives `core.autocrlf`? This does not affect the specs
  written here and can be decided in a later change.
- Should the offline HTML recognize the same warning titles as the
  website (`Caution`, `Important`, `Avertissement`, any case, a trailing
  `:`)? If so, that later change would modify the
  `Warning callouts in the offline HTML` requirement, and the comment in
  `docs.rs` would need to match.

# Proposal: Specify four behaviors that shipped without a spec

## Why

Four behaviors came in through ordinary pull requests and appear in no spec:
Windows (CRLF) line endings in decisions, warning callouts in the offline
HTML documentation, `codev docs --print` exiting quietly when its reader
goes away, and forward slashes in the inherited paths `codev init` writes.
The code and its tests already exist. Until the specs describe these
behaviors, nothing stops a later change from breaking them without anyone
noticing, so this change writes them into the specs, which are the
authoritative description of the project.

## What Changes

This change only documents behavior that already exists. It changes no
behavior, so no code changes and no new tests are needed.

- `decisions`: an ADR saved with CRLF line endings is read the same way as
  an LF one. Its body, which is what the seal hashes, starts right after the
  `---` line that closes the frontmatter, whatever its line ending. When
  `decision accept` rewrites the frontmatter of a CRLF file, the new
  frontmatter uses CRLF too and the body stays byte for byte identical.
- `docs`: in the offline HTML, a blockquote that opens on **Warning** or
  **Attention** in bold is shown as a warning callout, styled differently
  from a plain note. Any other blockquote stays a note.
- `docs`: when the reader of `codev docs --print` stops reading before the
  end (for example `codev docs --print | head`), the command exits with
  code 0 and writes nothing to stderr. Any other write error is still
  reported and the command exits with code 1.
- `init`: every relative local path that `--inherit` turns into an absolute
  path (a local folder, or a local git repository given by a relative path)
  is written to `config.yaml` with forward slashes on every platform.

Assumptions made without asking (an evaluation run, with no user to ask):

- The specs describe what the code does today. Where the code and its
  surroundings disagree, the spec follows the code, and the gap is listed
  as an open question in `design.md` without being fixed here. For example,
  the website theme recognizes more warning titles than the offline HTML
  does.
- Whether the seal normalizes line endings is left out of the specs on
  purpose (see `design.md`). Specifying that it does not would lock in a
  behavior that looks risky.
- "Slashes in inheritance paths" means the paths `codev init --inherit`
  writes to `config.yaml`. The JSON contract already uses `/` for every
  path, and that is a separate topic.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `decisions`
- `docs`
- `init`

### Removed Capabilities

## Impact

- Specs only: `_codev/specs/decisions`, `_codev/specs/docs` and
  `_codev/specs/init` gain requirements or scenarios. No code, JSON
  contract or dependency changes.
- Code these specs now describe: `codev-core` (ADR parser, seal body
  boundaries), `codev-engine` (frontmatter rewrite), `codev-cli` (`docs`
  rendering and `--print`, `init --inherit` path writing).
- User documentation (`docs/en`, `docs/fr`): no update. None of these
  behaviors is described in the user guide, and none needs to be.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: ADRs with Windows line endings

An ADR whose lines end in CRLF (for example a file saved or checked out on
Windows) SHALL be recognized exactly like the same ADR with LF line
endings: same fields, same findings. The body of a CRLF ADR, which is the
part the seal hashes, MUST start right after the `---` line that closes
the frontmatter, including that line's ending, as it does for an LF ADR.

When a command rewrites the frontmatter of a CRLF ADR (for example
`codev decision accept`, which changes its `status`), the rewritten
frontmatter MUST use CRLF line endings, and the body MUST stay byte for
byte identical. An LF ADR keeps LF line endings. A rewritten file never
mixes the two styles in its frontmatter or where the frontmatter meets the
body.

#### Scenario: A CRLF ADR is parsed like its LF version

- **GIVEN** two copies of the same ADR, one with LF line endings and one
  with CRLF line endings
- **WHEN** the parser reads both
- **THEN** both expose the same identifier, title, status, date and tags
- **AND** neither produces `decision_missing_frontmatter`

#### Scenario: Accepting a CRLF decision keeps its line endings and its body

- **GIVEN** a local ADR `0001` with `status: proposed`, saved with CRLF
  line endings
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev decision accept 0001`
- **THEN** the file now carries `status: accepted` followed by CRLF
- **AND** its body is identical, byte for byte, to what it was before the
  command
- **AND** no frontmatter line ends in a bare LF
- **AND** `codev validate` reports neither `decision_seal_mismatch` nor
  `decision_unsealed` for `0001`

#### Scenario: A CRLF file without a closing separator is still reported

- **GIVEN** a file that starts with a `---` line ending in CRLF but never
  closes its frontmatter with another `---` line
- **WHEN** the parser reads the file
- **THEN** it gets the same finding as an LF file with the same defect,
  and is not silently parsed

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Warning callouts in the offline HTML

In the HTML generated by `codev docs` (the default form and `--write`), a
blockquote whose first paragraph opens on the bold title `Warning` or
`Attention` (`> **Warning**`, `> **Attention**`) SHALL be rendered as a
**warning callout**. It MUST look different from a plain note, with its
own rule colour, background and title colour, using only the page's
inline CSS and no script.

Every other blockquote, including one that opens on another bold word
such as `**Note**`, MUST stay a plain note. Both titles are recognized in
both editions: either one can appear in the English or the French
documentation.

#### Scenario: Warning and Attention blockquotes become warning callouts

- **GIVEN** documentation containing `> **Warning**` followed by a
  sentence, then `> **Attention**` followed by a sentence
- **WHEN** the HTML is generated
- **THEN** both blockquotes are rendered as warning callouts
- **AND** the page stays self-contained (no external request, no
  required script)

#### Scenario: Other blockquotes stay notes

- **GIVEN** documentation containing `> **Note**` followed by a sentence,
  and a blockquote that does not open on a bold title
- **WHEN** the HTML is generated
- **THEN** both are rendered as plain notes, not as warning callouts

### Requirement: `codev docs --print` exits quietly when its reader goes away

When the program reading the output of `codev docs --print` closes it
before the end (for example `codev docs --print | head`), the command
SHALL stop, write nothing to stderr and exit with code 0. A reader that
has read enough is not an error.

Any other failure to write to stdout MUST still be reported on stderr as
`error: <reason>`, and the command MUST exit with code 1.

#### Scenario: Piping into a reader that stops early

- **GIVEN** the current binary
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --print | head -n 1`
- **THEN** `head` prints the first line of the documentation
- **AND** `codev` exits with code 0
- **AND** nothing is written to stderr

#### Scenario: Any other write failure is reported

- **GIVEN** a stdout that refuses writes for a reason other than the
  reader closing it (for example a full device)
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev docs --print`
- **THEN** stderr carries a line starting with `error: `
- **AND** the exit code is 1

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Inherited paths written by `codev init` use forward slashes

When `codev init --inherit` turns a relative source into an absolute path
before writing it to `_codev/config.yaml`, the written path SHALL use
forward slashes (`/`) as separators on every platform, Windows included,
and MUST NOT contain `.` or `..` segments. This applies to a relative
local folder (`path:`) and to a local git repository given by a relative
path (`git:`). The file is then identical whatever machine ran
`codev init`, and every other codev command can read it.

A source given as an absolute path, as a path starting with `~`, or as a
remote git URL is written exactly as given.

#### Scenario: A relative folder is written absolute, with forward slashes

- **GIVEN** a project at `/p` and an existing folder `/home/shared`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ../home/shared` from
  `/p`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `path: /home/shared`
- **AND** the written value contains neither `\` nor `..`

#### Scenario: On Windows, separators are forward slashes

- **GIVEN** a project at `C:\work\app` and an existing folder
  `C:\work\conventions`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ..\conventions` from
  `C:\work\app`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `path: C:/work/conventions`
- **AND** `codev status` and `codev sources list` read the file without
  error

#### Scenario: A relative local git repository is written with forward slashes

- **GIVEN** a project at `/p` and a local git repository
  `/p/vendor/conventions.git`
- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit
  vendor/conventions.git@v2` from `/p`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares
  `git: /p/vendor/conventions.git` with `ref: v2`

#### Scenario: A source given as `~` or as an absolute path is kept as given

- **WHEN** the user runs `codev init --yes --inherit ~/shared --inherit
  /home/shared`
- **THEN** `_codev/config.yaml` declares `path: ~/shared` and
  `path: /home/shared`, both unchanged
